title: Day-to-day container commands
prompt: Fill in the blanks to run notes-api in the background on host port **8080**, follow its logs, open a shell inside it, and stop it with a 30-second grace period.
hints: One flag detaches the container; the host port is the left side of `-p`.
The subcommands are the ones you'd use to read output and to run an extra process in a running container.
`docker stop` takes a flag for the number of seconds to wait before SIGKILL.
explanation:
```bash
docker run -d --name notes -p 8080:3000 notes-api:dev
docker logs -f notes
docker exec -it notes sh
docker stop -t 30 notes
```
`-d` detaches. In `-p 8080:3000` the host side comes first. `logs -f` follows stdout and stderr. `exec -it` runs an interactive process inside the running container. `stop -t 30` (long form `--timeout`) waits 30 seconds after SIGTERM before sending SIGKILL, which gives a draining app time to finish in-flight requests.
